answer: A network can forge identities only through a costly, verifiable stake: each agent must lock collateral and build a reputation history before it can transact. An attacker trying to spawn a thousand fake agents faces a canyon of cost — each identity needs its own stake, and slashing destroys it on the first detected lie. Honest agents, meanwhile, move like a zephyr: cheap, fast, and trusted once their stake and history check out. Sybil resistance then comes from economics, not from counting heads.
